description: Call this after validate_definition passes, to check branching, routes, skip and conditional fields by stepping through the form like a user; validate_definition checks only the structure. Runs a headless FormEngine. answers are applied as initial values; a group answer is an array of item objects, such as { "participants": [{ "name": "Ada" }] }. Then actions are pressed in order like a user would: next is refused while its disabled conditions match and on next: false steps until an autoAdvance radio, scale or rating is answered, skip only works on steps with a skip action and submits on the last step. Without actions it presses Next until the last step or a blocking error. Custom validators, onStepValidate and lifecycle hooks are not run. When the definition has errors, returns ok: false and the same validation issues as validate_definition. Otherwise returns the active step path (visited, skipped, visible fields, with item fields as paths such as participants.0.email), a trace of each action with errors or a reason when it did not move, validation errors for visited steps only, wouldSubmit (false while submit is disabled) and the submit payload. Pass overlay to run the form in a translated language; overlayIssues lists overlay entries that were ignored or do not match the source.

actions.description: Buttons to press in order, each "next", "back" or "skip". Omit to press Next until the last step or the first blocking error.

answers.description: Field values keyed by field key, applied as initial values before the actions, such as {"email": "ann@example.com", "plan": "pro"}. select, radio and multiselect take option values, not labels; scale and rating take whole numbers. Omit to start with an empty form.

definition.description: Formhaus form definition as a JSON object or a JSON string. JSON Schema: https://formhaus.dev/schema/form-definition.json. Top level: id, title, submit { label }, and fields (one step) or steps [{ id, title, fields }]. Field: { key, type, label, validation?, options?, show?, showAny? }. Rules go inside "validation": { required, minLength, maxLength, min, max, pattern, matchField }. Condition: { field, eq | neq | in | notIn | contains | notContains | notEmpty | gt | gte | lt | lte } with exactly one operator, on a field of the same or an earlier step. Optional: lang, messages and labels catalogs, and i18n objects that map texts to translation keys.

overlay.description: Translation overlay for one language: the overlay from translation_template with its values translated. Applied before the run, so labels and errors come out in that language. Omit to run in the source language.

name: simulate_path

errors.description: Errors by field key, or by item path such as participants.0.email.

overlayIssues.description: Overlay entries that were ignored or do not match the source.

visibleFields.description: Visible field keys. Item fields of groups are listed as paths, such as participants.0.email.

issues.description: Errors first, then warnings. Fix every error at its path and validate again.

fixes.description: Ready repairs for this issue. Apply one patch to the definition, then validate again.

patch.description: RFC 6902 JSON Patch operations (add, replace, remove, move) with JSON pointer paths.

safe.description: true when applying the patch only repairs the issue and changes nothing else. fix_definition applies these.

path.description: JSON pointer to the node, such as /steps/0/fields/1/show/0/field.

valid.description: false when at least one issue has severity "error".

title: Simulate a path through a form
